style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: A prayer of David, the first psalm titled simply 'a prayer,' and a courtroom appeal that turns into a plea for shelter. He asks God to hear a just case from deceitless lips, to let the verdict come from His own presence, and he reports the audit already done: You tested my heart, inspected me by night, refined me and found nothing -- a claim of innocence in this case, kept to the lips, not a claim of a sinless life. Then the petitions, with two of Scripture's tenderest images side by side: keep me as the apple of Your eye, hide me under the shadow of Your wings. The enemies are drawn as a lion longing to tear and a young lion crouched in hiding, and as men whose whole portion is in this life -- well fed by God Himself, full of sons, leaving their surplus to their babies. Against them David sets a different portion in the last verse: I will see Your face in righteousness; when I awake I will be satisfied with Your likeness. The church has never been able to read that line as only about tomorrow morning.

1.text: A prayer of David. Hear a just cause, O LORD; attend to my ringing cry; give ear to my prayer, which does not come from deceitful lips.
1.amp: A Prayer [tephillah] of David. Hear ['justice', tsedek, the KJV margin] the right, O LORD [YHWH], attend [qashab] unto my cry [rinnah -- ringing cry], give ear [azan] unto my prayer [tephillah], that goes not ['without lips of deceit', mirmah, the KJV margin] out of feigned lips [saphah].
1.notes: shimah YHWH tsedek (H8085, H3068, H6664): hear RIGHTEOUSNESS -- the margin's 'justice': David asks God to listen to a just case, the same courtroom opening as Psalm 26:1. haqshibah rinnati (H7181, H7440): attend to my rinnah, the ringing cry -- haazinah tephillati be-lo siphte mirmah (H238, H8605, H8193, H4820): give ear to a prayer 'without lips of deceit', the margin's literal. Three verbs for hearing: not doubt -- verse 6 says he calls because God answers -- but the urgency of a man whose case has not yet been tried.

2.text: Let my vindication come forth from Your presence; let Your eyes look on what is right.
2.amp: Let my sentence [mishpat -- judgment, vindication] come forth [yatsa] from Your presence [panim]; let Your eyes [ayin] behold [chazah] the things that are equal [meyshar -- upright].
2.notes: mi-le-phanekha mishpati yetse (H6440, H4941, H3318): let my verdict come out from before Your face -- not from the court of his enemies; enekha techezenah mesharim (H5869, H2372, H4339): let Your eyes see mesharim, the straight things. He wants the Judge to look, confident of what the look will find (cf. Psalm 11:4, 7).

3.text: You have tested my heart; You have visited me in the night; You have refined me and You find nothing; I have resolved that my mouth will not transgress.
3.amp: You have proved [bachan -- tested] mine heart [leb]; You have visited [paqad -- inspected] me in the night [layil]; You have tried [tsaraph -- refined] me, and shall find [matsa] nothing; I am purposed [zamam -- resolved] that my mouth [peh] shall not transgress [abar].
3.notes: bachanta libbi paqadta lailah tseraphtani bal-timtsa (H974, H3820, H6485, H3915, H6884, H4672): tested, inspected by night -- when a man is most himself -- refined, and nothing found: two of the three verbs of Psalm 26:2 -- bachan and tsaraph -- there prayed for, here reported as done, with paqad, the night inspection, added between them. zammoti bal-yaabor-pi (H2161, H5674, H6310): I have resolved my mouth will not cross the line. The claim is of a particular innocence in a particular case, not of a sinless life; verse 1 already said which -- the lips.

4.text: As for the works of men -- by the word of Your lips I have kept myself from the paths of the violent.
4.amp: Concerning the works [peullah] of men [adam], by the word [dabar] of Your lips [saphah] I have kept [shamar] me from the paths [orach] of the destroyer.
4.notes: li-pheullot adam bi-debar sephatekha (H6468, H120, H1697, H8193): as for what men do -- by the WORD of Your lips; ani shamarti orchot parits (H8104, H734): I have kept myself from the paths of the parits, the violent man, the housebreaker of Ezekiel 18:10. Note the two sets of lips: his deceitless ones (v. 1) and God's, whose word is the fence.

5.text: My steps have held fast to Your tracks; my feet have not slipped.
5.amp: Hold up [tamak -- uphold] my goings [ashur -- steps] in Your paths [magal -- wagon-tracks], that my footsteps [paam] slip ['be not moved', mot, the KJV margin] not.
5.notes: tamokh ashurai be-maggelotekha (H8551, H838, H4570): the KJV prays it (hold up my goings in Thy paths), the WEB reports it (my steps have held fast); the Hebrew infinitive allows either, and the two are one life; bal-namottu pheamai (H4131, H6471): my footfalls have not been 'moved', the margin's word. Kept in the ruts God made, the wheel does not slide.

6.text: I have called on You, for You will answer me, O God; bend Your ear to me and hear what I say.
6.amp: I have called [qara] upon You, for You will hear [anah -- answer] me, O God [El]: incline [natah] Your ear [ozen] unto me, and hear [shama] my speech [imrah].
6.notes: ani-qeratikha khi-taaneni El (H7121, H6030, H410): I have called BECAUSE You will answer -- the confidence is the reason for the prayer, not its result; hat-oznekha li shema imrati (H5186, H241, H8085, H565): tilt Your ear to me, hear my imrah, my saying. From the courtroom (vv. 1-5) to the ear: petition begins.

7.text: Show the wonder of Your covenant love, You who save those who take refuge from their assailants at Your right hand.
7.amp: Show Your marvellous [palah -- set-apart, wonderful] lovingkindness [chesed -- covenant love], O You that save [yasha] by Your right hand [yamin] them which put their trust [chasah -- take refuge] in You from those that rise up [qum] against them ['them which trust in thee from those that rise up against thy right hand', yamin, the KJV margin].
7.notes: haphleh chasadekha (H6395, H2617): make Your chesed, Your covenant love, WONDERFUL -- palah, the verb of setting apart, Exodus 8:22's Goshen. moshia chosim mi-mitqomemim bi-minekha (H3467, H2620, H6965, H3225): Savior of those taking refuge from their attackers -- 'at Your right hand', where the refuge is, or, as the margin reads, from those who rise 'against Your right hand'. Either way the right hand is the safe side.

8.text: Keep me as the apple of Your eye; under the shadow of Your wings hide me away,
8.amp: Keep [shamar] me as the apple [ishon -- the little man, the pupil] of the eye [bat ayin -- daughter of the eye], hide [satar] me under the shadow [tsel] of Your wings [kanaph],
8.notes: shomreni ke-ishon bat-ayin (H8104, H380, H1323, H5869): keep me as the ishon -- 'the little man', the reflection you see in someone's pupil -- the 'daughter of the eye', the Hebrew idiom for the pupil, the body's most guarded part (Deuteronomy 32:10). be-tsel kenaphekha tastireni (H6738, H3671, H5641): hide me in the shadow of Your wings -- the bird of Psalm 91:4, or the cherubim's wings over the ark. Two of the Bible's tenderest images in one verse, and Boaz's word for Ruth's refuge (Ruth 2:12).

9.text: from the wicked who lay me waste, my deadly enemies who close in around me.
9.amp: From [panim] the wicked [rasha] that [zu] oppress ['waste', shadad, the KJV margin] me, from my deadly enemies ['my enemies against the soul', nephesh, the KJV margin], who compass me about.
9.notes: mi-pene reshaim zu shadduni (H6440, H7563, H2098, H7703): from the wicked who have DEVASTATED me -- shadad, the margin's 'waste', the word for a razed field; oyebai be-nephesh yaqqiphu alai (H341, H5315): my 'enemies against the soul', the margin's literal -- enemies after my life -- who encircle me. The refuge of verse 8 is needed because the ring of verse 9 is closing.

10.text: They have shut up their callous hearts; with their mouths they speak arrogantly.
10.amp: They are inclosed [sagar -- shut up] in their own fat [cheleb]: with their mouth [peh] they speak [dabar] proudly [geut -- loftily].
10.notes: chelbamo sageru (H2459, H5462): 'their fat they have closed' -- the fat around the heart as the Hebrew picture of insensibility (Psalm 119:70; Deuteronomy 32:15), a man so well-fed he cannot feel; pimo dibberu be-geut (H6310, H1696, H1348): their mouth speaks in geut, the majesty-word of Psalm 93:1 stolen for a sneer.

11.text: At our every step they have now surrounded us; they fix their eyes on throwing us to the ground,
11.amp: They have now compassed [sabab -- surrounded] us in our steps [ashur]: they have set [shith] their eyes [ayin] bowing down [natah -- to cast down] to the earth [eretz];
11.notes: ashurenu attah sebabunu (H838, H5437): our steps -- now they have surrounded us: the same ashur God was asked to hold up in verse 5; enehem yashitu lintot ba-aretz (H5869, H7896, H5186, H776): they set their eyes to stretch us out on the ground -- the hunter's stare before the throw. The plural 'us' widens the prayer: David is not the only one in the ring.

12.text: He is like a lion that longs to tear, like a young lion crouched in hiding.
12.amp: Like ['The likeness of him is as a lion that desireth to ravin', dimyon, the KJV margin] as a lion [aryeh] that is greedy [kasaph -- longs] of his prey [tereph -- torn flesh], and as it were a young lion [kephir] lurking ['sitting', yashab, the KJV margin] in secret places.
12.notes: dimyono ke-aryeh yikhsoph litroph (H738, H3700, H2963): 'his likeness', the margin's literal -- like a lion that LONGS to tear -- kasaph, to grow pale with craving; ve-khi-khphir yoshev be-mistarim (H3715, H3427): and like a young lion SITTING in hiding, the margin's word. Psalm 10:8-9's predator -- the same yashab ('he sitteth', 10:8) and the same mistar, the hiding place (10:9): the wicked sit in ambush the way God sits enthroned -- one waiting to kill, One waiting to judge.

13.text: Arise, O LORD! Confront him, bring him down; rescue my soul from the wicked man by Your sword,
13.amp: Arise [qum], O LORD [YHWH], disappoint ['prevent his face', qadam, the KJV margin] him, cast him down [kara -- make him kneel]: deliver [palat] my soul [nephesh] from the wicked [rasha], which is Your sword ['by thy sword', cherev, the KJV margin]:
13.notes: qumah YHWH qaddemah phanav hakhriehu (H6965, H3068, H6923, H6440, H3766): rise, LORD -- 'go before his face', the margin's literal, meet him head-on -- make him KNEEL; palletah naphshi me-rasha charbekha (H6403, H5315, H7563, H2719): rescue my soul from the wicked -- 'Your sword'. Read one way the wicked man is God's own sword, His instrument, as Assyria is His rod (Isaiah 10:5); read with the margin, David is rescued 'by Your sword'. Either reading leaves the wicked in God's hand.

14.text: from men, by Your hand, O LORD, from men of this world whose portion is in this life -- whose bellies You fill with what You have stored up; they have their fill of sons and leave what is left to their children.
14.amp: From men which are Your hand ['by thy hand', yad, the KJV margin], O LORD [YHWH], from men of the world [cheled -- this fleeting age], which have their portion [cheleq] in this life [chay], and whose belly [beten] You fill [male] with Your hid treasure: they are full ['their children are full', saba, the KJV margin] of children [ben], and leave [yanach] the rest [yether] of their substance to their babes.
14.notes: mi-metim yadekha YHWH mi-metim me-cheled (H3027, H3068, H2465): from men -- 'by Your hand', the margin -- men of cheled, the passing world, chelqam ba-chayyim (H2506, H2416): whose portion is in this life only -- one of the sharpest descriptions of worldliness in the Psalter: not wicked pleasures but a share that ends at death. u-tsephunkha temalle bitnam (H6840, H4390, H990): You fill their belly with Your stored-up goods -- God feeds them too. yisbeu banim (H7646, H1121): they are sated with sons, ve-hinnichu yitram le-olelehem (H3240, H3499, H5768): and leave their surplus to their babies. Verse 15 answers with a different portion.

15.text: As for me, I will see Your face in righteousness; when I awake, I will be satisfied with Your likeness.
15.amp: As for me, I will behold [chazah] Your face [panim] in righteousness [tsedek]: I shall be satisfied [saba], when I awake [quts], with Your likeness.
15.notes: ani be-tsedek echezeh phanekha (H6664, H2372, H6440): 'I' -- the emphatic pronoun against the men of verse 14 -- will gaze on Your face in righteousness. esbeah be-haqits temunatekha (H7646, H6974, H8544): I will be SATISFIED -- the same saba the worldly get from sons -- on waking, with Your temunah, Your form, the word for what Moses saw (Numbers 12:8). Whether the waking is tomorrow's or the resurrection's, the church has read it as both: Psalm 16:11 and 1 John 3:2 in one line.
